name: file-uploads

envVars.STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL: Origin a public object is served from — an R2 custom domain in production (https://files.example.com), or this api's own origin in dev. The object key is appended to it verbatim, so it holds an origin and never a path. Leave it unset and `POST /files/uploads` refuses `visibility: "public"` with a message naming this variable; nothing falls back to private.
envVars.STORAGE_IMAGE_TRANSFORMS: Set to `true` when Cloudflare image transformations are enabled on the zone serving STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL. Default off, because the `/cdn-cgi/image/` prefix 404s on a zone that has not turned them on. With it off `publicImageUrl` returns the plain public URL and ignores its options, so every image still renders.
envVars.STORAGE_PURGE_AFTER_DAYS: Days a soft-deleted row is kept before the sweep drops it. Defaults to 30. Read only by the sweep job, so it does nothing in a project without the `queue` capability. A value that is not a positive whole number throws on the first tick.

removeWarnings: The deployed storage_objects table survives this removal. Run db:generate and review the resulting drop migration before you apply it.

The objects themselves survive it too. They have no lifecycle rule, so every key under t/<tenantId>/uploads/ and t/<tenantId>/public-uploads/ stays in the bucket until you delete it with `wrangler r2 object delete`.
A public object's URL keeps working for as long as the bytes are there. Removing this module removes the record, not the access.
